title: Security: 9 trust-header reads outside auth middleware (pen-test F-04) — surfaced by wiring check-no-trust-header-reads.sh in KS-926
description:
**Found by RUNNING a guard that had never run.** KS-926 wired the `check-*.sh` guards; this one had no live entry point, so its findings had never been seen. Its default level is `fail`, so it is red the moment anything invokes it.

## The 9, verbatim from the guard

```
services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1041  req.headers['x-tenant-id']
services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1042  req.headers['x-tenant-slug']
services/security/src/index.ts:968                    req.headers['x-tenant-id']
services/prism/src/index.ts:111                       req.headers['x-tenant-id']
services/originate/src/index.ts:230                   req.headers['x-tenant-id']
services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts:42          req.headers['x-user-role'] === 'connector' && x-tenant-id
services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts:43          req.headers['x-user-id']  -> sets (req as any).user
services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts:45          req.headers['x-tenant-id'] -> sets (req as any).tenantId
packages/shared/src/db/tenant-guc.ts:119              req.headers['x-tenant-id']
```

`metering.ts:42-45` **is the one to look at first:** it builds `req.user` and `req.tenantId` **from headers**, gated only on `x-user-role === 'connector'`. That is the trust-header vulnerability in its literal form if the header is reachable from outside.

## The guard's own instruction

> Use `req.user.*` (set by `authenticate()` middleware) instead of `req.headers['x-user-*']`. Direct header reads re-introduce the trust-header vulnerability.

The guard already excludes legitimate middleware paths (`/middleware/auth.ts`, `authenticate.ts`, `scopes.ts`, `tenant*`, `db/tenant-context.ts`, `security/gdpr-compliance.ts`) and lines marked `F-04-allowed`, so **these 9 are outside the sanctioned set by the guard's own definition.**

## Triage needed per site

Some may be legitimate **forwarding** (api-gateway 1041-42 sets `forwardHeaders`, which is a different act from trusting) and should carry `F-04-allowed` with a reason. Others look like real trust. **Do not bulk-annotate** — that converts a finding into a silence.

## Blocks

`check-no-trust-header-reads.sh` cannot be wired into the pre-push gate until this is 0 or the legitimate sites are annotated. Related: KS-619 (gateway tenant resolution falling through to the caller's `x-tenant-id`), and KS-926.

nodes.title: KS-1032: originate stops trusting a trust header it cannot attribute to the gateway

nodes.body:
**KS-1600** carries an open question against this ticket's effect. The pull request 1547 round-2 gate (report `ccbe317fcbf769f3`) measured that a forged `x-tenant-id` sent **directly to originate's router** is honoured — `ORG_ADMIN(A1)` + `organizations:register` + `organizationId: A1` with `x-tenant-id: T2` returns 201 with the key stored in tenant T2. The gate's reading is that KS-1032, now on `develop` `92d1316ffe31cb13b3f7e843e7891225383b2f84`, shuts that path, because `gatewayProvenance` strips trust headers when `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is unset and the KS-458 resolution reads `x-tenant-id` only on a vouched request. **That is a reading, not a measurement** — the gate's harness mounts the router without `index.ts`'s middleware, so it was never run end to end.

The instrument that would settle it, recorded on KS-1600: one end-to-end request through originate's real middleware stack on `develop` `92d1316f`, `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` unset, forged `x-tenant-id: T2`, expecting the key to land in the caller's own tenant rather than T2.

Facts only; no state change asked for here.

## BLUF

- **Recorded from KS-1041, so this residual stays on a live ticket when KS-1041 closes.** KS-1041 wrote down that services other than originate also read trust headers, and that nobody had read their sites.
- **This ticket is the live home for that class:** trust-header reads outside auth middleware, triaged per site.
- **Not commissioned and not ruled.** KS-1041's two steps did not widen to these services.
  - Step 1: #938 → `0f8fb33c3` closed nginx `/originate/`.
  - Step 2: #951 is originate's gateway-provenance middleware. It stays inert while `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is unset (KS-1083).

## Recommendation

No action needed now. When this ticket's per-site triage runs, include the services KS-1041 named.

## Detail

- **KS-1041's wording, verbatim:**
  - `923cfb00` (2026-09-10): *"`api-gateway`, `auth`, `billing`, `prism`, `security` and `tokenisation` also read these headers. **I am not asserting they are safe — I have not read their sites.**"*
  - `116ed2d6`, and PR #951's *Not in scope*: *"the seven other services that read trust headers"*.
  - Six are named and "seven" is counted. Both are quoted as written; neither was re-measured here.
- **Overlap with this ticket's 9 sites:**
  - api-gateway, security and prism appear in both.
  - auth, billing and tokenisation do not appear here. This ticket's guard excludes middleware paths (`/middleware/auth.ts`, `authenticate.ts`, `tenant*`, and others), which may be why — not checked.
  - `originate/src/index.ts:230` and `routes/metering.ts:42-45` are the originate sites that #951's middleware covers once the secret is provisioned. Until then they behave as before.
- **Board searched before posting** (literal, live tickets only):
  - `trust headers` → KS-1041 only;
  - `x-user-role` → KS-1041 and KS-1032;
  - `x-tenant-id` → 8, of which KS-1032 is the only one about reads across services;
  - `header-reading` 0 · `seven other` 0.
